description: Citizenship in the World explores what it means to be a citizen of a connected world: how people become U.S. citizens, how nations pursue their interests, international law and trade, kinds of government, diplomacy, and connecting with people from other countries.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Requirements 6 and 7 changed for 2026; requirement 6 became three required parts.

requirements.title: World citizenship
requirements.summary: What world citizenship means to you and what it takes to be a good world citizen.

requirements.title: Becoming a citizen
requirements.summary: How people become U.S. citizens, the rights, duties and obligations of citizenship, and how they compare with other countries.

requirements.title: National interest and economies
requirements.summary: A current world event and national interest, and how a country’s geography and resources shape its economy.

children.title: National interest
children.summary: How national interest affects a country’s actions in a current world event.

children.title: Geography and economy
children.summary: How a foreign country’s geography, natural resources and climate shape its economy and partnerships.

requirements.title: International relations
requirements.summary: Options covering international and national law, a current trade issue, and international organizations.

requirements.title: Kinds of government
requirements.summary: Options covering constitutional and non-constitutional governments and governments in power today.

requirements.title: Diplomacy
requirements.summary: How governments are represented abroad, the roles of ambassadors and consuls, and passports and visas.

children.title: Representation abroad
children.summary: How governments are represented in other countries.

children.title: Ambassadors and consuls
children.summary: The roles of ambassadors, consuls and other diplomats.

children.title: Passports and visas
children.summary: The purpose of passports and visas.

requirements.title: Connecting with the world
requirements.summary: Options such as visiting the State Department’s website, meeting a Scout or student from another country, or taking part in an international event.
